sarah.dev: Hey folks — hitting flaky NDJSON streaming in the Kotlin client when we publish a shaded fat jar (OkHttp relocated + Jackson shaded). Server emits continuous NDJSON but client stalls after a few seconds intermittently. Repro locally.
raj.patel: How are you performing the shading? Relocate rules or merging packages?
sarah.dev: Using Gradle Shadow: relocate 'okhttp3' to 'com.redwood.shadow.okhttp3' and 'com.fasterxml.jackson.databind' to 'com.redwood.shadow.jackson.databind'. No merges configured initially.
mike_h: Two quick suspects: (1) ServiceLoader resources for OkHttp may be duplicated/removed during shading, (2) okhttp3.internal classes not relocated causing mixed-class references.
jenna: Also check interceptor ordering. If auth or timeout logic ends up as a different classloader package it might not be invoked on the streaming path.
sarah.dev: Example client code:

sarah.dev: ```kotlin
val client = OkHttpClient.Builder()
  .addInterceptor(AuthInterceptor(token))
  .addNetworkInterceptor(LoggingInterceptor())
  .readTimeout(0, TimeUnit.MILLISECONDS)
  .connectionPool(ConnectionPool(5, 5, TimeUnit.MINUTES))
  .build()
```

sarah.dev: Even with readTimeout(0) streams stop after ~8-15s, no error, just hang.
raj.patel: Run the jar tool and inspect shaded jar: jar tf build/libs/*.jar | grep okhttp3. If you see both okhttp3 and com/redwood/shadow/... variants, you might have leftover originals.
mike_h: For Shadow plugin, make sure to use ServiceFileTransformer to merge META-INF/services files, and relocate okhttp3.internal. e.g.

mike_h: ```gradle
shadowJar {
  relocate 'okhttp3', 'com.redwood.shadow.okhttp3'
  relocate 'okio', 'com.redwood.shadow.okio'
  transform(ServiceFileTransformer)
}
```

jenna: For Jackson make sure the Kotlin & JavaTime modules are registered against the relocated ObjectMapper. If module classes are still referencing original package names module discovery can fail.
raj.patel: Quick debug trick: add a tiny interceptor at the top of the chain that logs a numeric step tag when request enters and when response returns. If you never see the step logs that means the interceptor chain is being short-circuited.
oliver: Also try running the same code with non-shaded dependencies on classpath (no relocation) to confirm shading is the variable. If streaming works there it's shading-related.
ci-bot: CI: client.integrationTest failed on streaming-case (build 3478) — posting logs: [link]
sarah.dev: Ran without shading — stable. So shading introduces the regressions.
jenna: Additional pitfall: if you relocate okhttp but third-party libs still compile against okhttp3 and packaged references to internal classes, some bytecode might still point to okhttp3.internal.* which won't match relocated ones. Use broad relocate patterns to catch internals.
mike_h: Another thing: check ConnectionPool sizes after shading — I've seen defaulting back to tiny pool because the builder instance used at runtime was from a different (unrelocated) class and configs didn't apply.
raj.patel: For validation: run `strings`/`grep` against the shaded jar to ensure only one okhttp package appears and inspect META-INF/services/okhttp3.internal... files are present and merged.
sarah.dev: Thanks — updated shadow rules to also relocate 'okhttp3.internal.**' and added ServiceFileTransformer + merging for META-INF/services. Also forced explicit ObjectMapper.registerModule(KotlinModule()) in our client lib.
sarah.dev: Quick follow-up: after that the minimal repro stream stayed open and NDJSON read progressed. I'll open a PR with the changed shadow config and add a small integration that asserts streaming Liveness.
oliver: Nice. If you want I can review the PR and run it against full integration suite.
sarah.dev: Appreciate it — will ping once PR is up. :thumbsup:
